nom-rau-don-lai-chau.name: Lai Chau Thai Fern Salad
nom-rau-don-lai-chau.serving_basis: One shared salad for four, served with rice or grilled dishes.
nom-rau-don-lai-chau.description: Young edible fern shoots are lightly wilted, steamed, then tossed with ginger, garlic, fresh herbs, lime and roasted peanuts. Bếp Việt edits this into a bright home-style side while retaining the steaming method associated with Thai cooking in Lai Chau.
nom-rau-don-lai-chau.finished_dish: Tender-crisp green ferns with a naturally nutty taste, gently sour lime, fragrant ginger and garlic, and roasted peanuts.
nom-rau-don-lai-chau.serving: Add the peanuts just before serving to preserve their crunch. Serve with steamed rice, grilled fish or a main dish, and eat soon after mixing.
tips: Choose young ferns from a trusted food source; trim tough stems, rinse well and drain.
Steam rather than boil to retain the color and texture; do not pack the shoots tightly into the steamer.
Add lime, salt and chili gradually so their flavors do not overwhelm the fern.
nom-rau-don-lai-chau.image_alt: Lai Chau fern salad with young green shoots, herbs, roasted peanuts and chili on a ceramic plate; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
nom-rau-don-lai-chau.time_note: About 45 minutes, including 10 minutes to wilt the fern and 20 minutes to steam it.

ingredients.name: Young fern shoots
ingredients.notes: Choose tender shoots from a trusted food source; remove tough stems.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Lightly crush, leaving some larger pieces for garnish.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese balm
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop or pound.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Finely chop; reduce or omit to taste.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Strain out the seeds and adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season gradually.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Optional; add only to soften the sourness.

preparation_steps: Trim the fern shoots, discard tough stems, rinse well and drain. Air-dry or briefly sun-wilt for about 10 minutes until slightly limp.
Chop the ginger, garlic and chili; chop the cilantro and Vietnamese balm. Roast the peanuts if needed and crush them.
cooking_steps: Arrange the fern in a steamer and steam for about 20 minutes, until tender but still green. Remove and let it cool slightly.
Mix the ginger, garlic, chili, lime juice, salt and sugar. Taste for a gently sour, lightly salted balance.
Place the warm fern in a bowl, add the herbs and dressing, and toss gently. Rest for about 5 minutes, then top with peanuts and serve.

canh-uoi-nguoi-thai-thanh-hoa.name: Thai Canh Uôi Rice, Fish and Bamboo Soup (Thanh Hoa)
aliases: Thanh Hoa Thai rice, fish and bamboo soup
canh-uoi-nguoi-thai-thanh-hoa.serving_basis: One lightly thickened pot of soup for four, served with steamed rice.
canh-uoi-nguoi-thai-thanh-hoa.description: Canh uôi from the Thai communities of Thanh Hoa combines rice, small stream fish and fresh bamboo shoots in a broth between soup and porridge. Bếp Việt edits the home method to keep the fish's savory flavor and the bamboo's gentle bite.
canh-uoi-nguoi-thai-thanh-hoa.finished_dish: A lightly thickened soup with rice blended through the broth, small whole fish cooked through and tender-crisp bamboo shoots, finished with herbs and optional mắc khén.
canh-uoi-nguoi-thai-thanh-hoa.serving: Ladle hot soup into bowls, dividing the fish and bamboo evenly. Serve with plain rice; offer toasted ground mắc khén separately.
tips: Soak the rice until soft, then grind it finely; stir continuously as it enters the pot to prevent lumps.
Season the fish lightly with salt and add it after the soup returns to a boil; simmer gently until cooked through.
Add hot water if the soup thickens too much; the finished texture should be between soup and porridge.
canh-uoi-nguoi-thai-thanh-hoa.image_alt: A bowl of Thanh Hoa canh uôi with small stream fish, bamboo-shoot strands and herbs in lightly thickened broth; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
canh-uoi-nguoi-thai-thanh-hoa.time_note: About 2 hours 55 minutes, including 2 hours to soak the rice.

ingredients.name: Plain rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse, soak for 2 hours, then pound or grind finely.

ingredients.name: Small freshwater fish
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh small fish; clean the gills and entrails. They may be cooked whole.

ingredients.name: Fresh bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Use food-grade shoots; slice thinly, soak in lightly salted water and rinse.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the soup; add more hot water if needed.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Toasted mắc khén
ingredients.notes: Grind finely and use to taste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between seasoning the fish and the soup.

ingredients.name: Monosodium glutamate
ingredients.notes: Optional; may be omitted.

preparation_steps: Rinse the rice and soak it in clean water for 2 hours until soft, then pound or grind it into a fine slurry.
Clean the fish and season with about 1 g salt for 10 minutes. Slice the bamboo shoots thinly, soak in lightly salted water and rinse; chop the scallions and cilantro.
cooking_steps: Bring the water to a boil, add the bamboo shoots and cook for about 15 minutes until tender and less pungent.
Stir the rice slurry with a little cold water until pourable. Add it gradually while stirring, then simmer until the soup returns to a boil and begins to thicken.
Add the fish, reduce the heat and simmer gently for about 20 minutes until fully cooked. Avoid stirring hard so the fish stays whole.
Season with the remaining salt and optional MSG. Add scallions, cilantro and mắc khén, then turn off the heat once the herbs smell fragrant.

reu-da-nuong-lai-chau.name: Lai Chau Thai Grilled Stream Moss
reu-da-nuong-lai-chau.serving_basis: Four portions of grilled stream moss, served as a vegetable side with rice.
reu-da-nuong-lai-chau.description: Edible stream moss is rinsed and pounded to remove grit, squeezed dry, seasoned with lemongrass, ginger, chili and highland spices, then wrapped in dong leaves and grilled. Bếp Việt adapts the dish into small parcels that cook evenly at home.
reu-da-nuong-lai-chau.finished_dish: Soft, slightly chewy and moist moss scented with lemongrass, ginger, mắc khén and grilled leaves; the leaves are darkened while the filling stays unburnt.
reu-da-nuong-lai-chau.serving: Unwrap the outer leaves and eat the moss hot with steamed rice and a main dish. Use only moss identified and sold as food from a trusted source; do not forage from water of unknown quality.
tips: Use only stream moss positively identified as edible and sold as food; avoid moss from polluted or unknown water sources.
Rinse and pound it repeatedly on a clean surface to remove grit, then squeeze it very dry so the parcels do not turn soggy.
Grill at a moderate distance from the coals and turn evenly; open one parcel to check that the center is hot and cooked before serving.
reu-da-nuong-lai-chau.image_alt: Lai Chau grilled stream moss in a partly opened dong-leaf parcel on a ceramic plate; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
reu-da-nuong-lai-chau.time_note: About 45 minutes for cleaning, seasoning and grilling.

ingredients.name: Cleaned edible stream moss
ingredients.notes: Use only a positively identified edible variety sold as food; drain well.

ingredients.name: Dong leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse and dry; use a second leaf if they are thin.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Rinse and finely chop the tender part.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Chili powder
ingredients.notes: Reduce or omit to taste.

ingredients.name: Toasted mắc khén
ingredients.notes: Lightly toast and grind.

ingredients.name: Toasted dổi seeds
ingredients.notes: Grind finely and use sparingly.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season gradually.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: A small amount helps keep the filling moist while grilling.

preparation_steps: Spread the moss in a basket and rinse it repeatedly with clean water. Place it on a clean board, gently pound it a few times with a wooden pestle, rinse again until grit is gone, then squeeze it very dry.
Chop the lemongrass and ginger. Lightly toast and grind the mắc khén and dổi seeds; mix with the chili powder, salt and oil.
cooking_steps: Toss the moss with the seasoning mixture and rest for about 5 minutes. Divide into four portions, place on dong leaves and fold into flat, sealed parcels.
Grill the parcels on a rack about 8–10 minutes per side over moderate charcoal, turning evenly. Alternatively, bake at 200°C for about 18–20 minutes, turning halfway.
When the leaves are darkened and the filling is hot and cooked through, remove from the heat and rest for 2 minutes. Open one parcel to check before serving.

mang-nom-hoa-ban-lai-chau.name: Lai Chau Bamboo Shoot and Ban Flower Salad
aliases: Bamboo shoot and ban flower salad
Thai-style bitter bamboo and ban flower salad
mang-nom-hoa-ban-lai-chau.serving_basis: One spring salad for four, served as a starter or with rice.
mang-nom-hoa-ban-lai-chau.description: A seasonal salad of the Thai people in Lai Chau combines thoroughly boiled bitter bamboo shoots, ban flower petals and flaked grilled stream fish. Bếp Việt edits the lime, garlic, chili and herb seasoning into a balanced home recipe with nutty, gently sour notes.
mang-nom-hoa-ban-lai-chau.finished_dish: Crisp bamboo-shoot strips, delicate ban petals and sweet grilled fish, tossed with lime, garlic, chili, herbs and roasted peanuts.
mang-nom-hoa-ban-lai-chau.serving: Toss just before serving so the flowers and herbs stay fresh. Serve as a first course or with upland sticky rice or cơm lam.
tips: Use only ban flowers positively identified as edible and sourced from a trusted grower; pick the thicker petals, rinse gently and drain.
Soak the bitter bamboo shoots in salted water, boil them twice and discard both cooking waters before draining and tossing.
Grill the fish until fully cooked, then carefully remove the bones; mix the salad immediately before serving.
search_terms: bitter bamboo and ban flower salad
mang-nom-hoa-ban-lai-chau.image_alt: Lai Chau măng nộm hoa ban with pale violet flower petals, bamboo shoots, grilled fish, herbs and peanuts; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
mang-nom-hoa-ban-lai-chau.time_note: About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 30 minutes to soak the bamboo shoots.

ingredients.name: Bitter bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Use food-grade shoots; slice into strips, soak in salted water and boil thoroughly twice.

ingredients.name: Edible ban flower petals
ingredients.notes: Choose clean petals from a trusted source; pick thicker petals, rinse gently and drain.

ingredients.name: Fresh stream fish
ingredients.notes: Clean, grill until fully cooked, then flake the flesh and check for bones.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Lightly crush.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese balm
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Chop or slice; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Strain out the seeds.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add gradually so it does not overwhelm the flower and bamboo.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For soaking the bamboo and seasoning the dressing.

preparation_steps: Slice the bitter bamboo shoots into bite-size strips and soak in lightly salted water for about 30 minutes. Gently rinse the ban petals; chop the garlic, chili, Vietnamese balm and cilantro.
Clean the stream fish and prepare a grill. Roast the peanuts if needed, then lightly crush them.
cooking_steps: Discard the soaking water. Boil the bamboo shoots for about 10 minutes, discard the water, then boil again for 10–15 minutes until cooked. Drain thoroughly.
Grill the fish over charcoal or in a grill pan until the flesh is opaque and separates easily from the bones. Flake the flesh and check carefully for bones.
Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, garlic, chili and a little salt. Place the bamboo, flower petals, fish and herbs in a bowl.
Add the dressing gradually and toss gently. Taste, top with roasted peanuts and serve immediately.

nhua-pho-thit-bam-goi-la-nuong-tay-bac.name: Northwest Thai Nhứa Pho Leaf-Wrapped Grilled Pork
nhua-pho-thit-bam-goi-la-nuong-tay-bac.serving_basis: Four grilled pork parcels, served with rice or upland sticky rice.
nhua-pho-thit-bam-goi-la-nuong-tay-bac.description: Nhứa pho is minced pork mixed with fragrant lemongrass, ginger, garlic and mắc khén, wrapped in dong or banana leaves and grilled over charcoal. Bếp Việt divides it into smaller parcels for even cooking while keeping the tender meat and toasted leaf aroma.
nhua-pho-thit-bam-goi-la-nuong-tay-bac.finished_dish: Dark-golden leaf parcels hold tender minced pork fragrant with lemongrass, ginger, shallot, garlic and mắc khén; moist inside and not charred.
nhua-pho-thit-bam-goi-la-nuong-tay-bac.serving: Serve hot with plain rice or upland sticky rice. Open the parcels at the table and use a clean plate; never return cooked pork to a plate that held raw meat.
tips: Choose pork shoulder with a little fat so the mince stays moist; marinate for about 15 minutes.
Use two or three layers of dong or banana leaves and keep each parcel moderately thin so the center cooks through.
Grill a moderate distance from the coals and turn often; ground pork should reach at least 71°C in the center.
search_terms: mắc khén grilled pork in dong leaves
nhua-pho-thit-bam-goi-la-nuong-tay-bac.image_alt: Northwest Thai nhứa pho on a ceramic plate, with a golden grilled dong-leaf parcel opened to show seasoned minced pork; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
nhua-pho-thit-bam-goi-la-nuong-tay-bac.time_note: About 1 hour, including 15 minutes to marinate the pork.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: Choose a cut with some fat; mince by hand or grind coarsely.

ingredients.name: Dong leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse and dry; banana leaves may be substituted.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Rinse and finely chop the tender part.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and chop.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and chop.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and chop.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Toasted mắc khén
ingredients.notes: Lightly toast and grind.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Chop; optional.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season gradually to account for its saltiness.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season lightly.

preparation_steps: Coarsely mince the pork shoulder. Chop the lemongrass, shallot, garlic, ginger, scallions and herbs.
Mix the pork with the seasonings and mắc khén, then marinate for 15 minutes. Rinse and dry the dong leaves; cut them to a size suitable for wrapping.
cooking_steps: Divide the pork into four flat portions. Place each portion on two or three layers of leaves and fold into a sealed rectangle; secure with a toothpick if needed.

Grill over moderately hot coals for about 10–12 minutes per side, turning evenly until the leaves are dark golden but not charred. Alternatively, bake at 200°C for about 20–25 minutes, turning halfway.
Check the thickest portion with a food thermometer; it should reach at least 71°C. Rest for 2 minutes, open the parcels and serve hot.
